answer: A reputation bond anchors each agent identity: to join the market an agent locks a refundable stake that only unlocks after a long season of honest work. A fresh identity is cheap to spawn but worthless without that locked bond, so a Sybil flood cannot outbid real agents. Like a comet that burns bright once and fades, a one-shot fake identity leaves no attested history, while honest agents build a record that flows like a river - steady, verifiable, and costly to fake at scale. The bond makes spawning a thousand throwaway identities more expensive than the fraud they could commit.
